title: fix(console): a settings page asks before leaving with unsaved edits (objectui#13163)
body:
Fixes #13163

Clause-②: no

## What was broken

Measured on the card (Setup, Localization): change Default country so the bar reads "1 unsaved change", click *Company* in the sidebar, and the console navigated at once; the edit was gone. `SettingsView`, the one renderer behind every `system/settings/:namespace` page, keeps its edits in a component-state draft, and nothing stood between that draft and a departure.

## What changed

- **New `apps/console/src/pages/settings/useUnsavedLeaveGuard.ts`**, local to the console app; no published export moves. While armed it installs a `beforeunload` listener (tab close, reload) and a capture-phase `click` listener on the document for a same-origin link to another pathname, and it returns `confirmLeave(go)` for the page's own navigations. Both listeners come off when the page goes clean (save, Discard) or unmounts. It follows `ResourceEditPage`'s guard (same skips: a modified or non-primary click, a `target` other than `_self`, `download`, another origin, the same pathname).
- **`SettingsView` arms it exactly while the "N unsaved changes" bar is drawn**: a loaded page with at least one edit, not the skeleton and not the error card. Its "All settings" crumb now goes through `confirmLeave`.
- **The prompt asks the existing `form.unsavedChanges`** ("You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to leave?"), which all ten packs already hold. No i18n key is added and no string moves.
- `.changeset/13163-settings-leave-guard.md`, `@object-ui/console` patch.

### Why `window.confirm`, not the record form's in-app dialog

The card's expected behaviour is a guard, and it names the record form's "Discard changes?" dialog as the one it saw. An in-app dialog is asynchronous, so the link guard would have to cancel every click and then navigate again for the user once they agree. Each way of doing that breaks something here:

1. Re-dispatching the click on the stored anchor is the synthetic-trigger shape ADR-0054 C1 bans ("the mouse equivalent that queries a node and dispatches click").
2. Calling `navigate(anchor.href)` instead has to strip the router basename that a host's injected base-href tag sets (the console resolves `BrowserRouter`'s basename from it), or it doubles the prefix. It also drops the link's own `onClick` (the mobile sidebar's home link closes the sheet in its `onClick`), its `replace` and its `state`. And it turns a plain same-origin anchor's document load into an SPA push.

A synchronous `confirm` needs none of that: on OK the click carries on untouched. The Setup app's other page-leave guards already use it (`ResourceEditPage` and `StudioDesignSurface`), while the record form's dialog closes an overlay and never has to navigate. The sentence is a leave question, not the form's "If you close this form now", which would be wrong on a page.

## Measurements (dispatch hypotheses H1 to H4)

- **H1, the producer: confirmed, with one correction.** Real Chromium at the base commit `c209c93` (scratch probe, below): a sidebar link went to the other page at once, a link to another namespace loaded it with the edit gone, the "All settings" crumb went to the hub at once, and a tab close with an edit closed with no prompt. All of these happened without a dialog. **Correction:** the error card's `navigate(-1)` is not a way to lose an edit. That card renders only after a failed load, which draws no fields and no save bar, so there is nothing on screen to lose. It stays unguarded on purpose, and the guard is disarmed there. A namespace-to-namespace move keeps the same `SettingsView` mounted. The draft survives the URL change and is reset only when the new namespace's load succeeds (read from `load`, which clears it on success only). So it was lost on that path too, and the guard now covers it as a link to another pathname.
- **H2, the fix shape:** followed, with `window.confirm` chosen for the reasons above.
- **H3, controls:** all hold. There is no prompt on a clean page, after a successful save, after Discard, for a same-pathname link, for a ctrl, meta or middle click, for a new-tab link, for a download, or for another origin. Cancel keeps both the URL and the draft ("1 unsaved change", the box still reads the edit). OK navigates and the edit goes with the page. The listeners are gone after unmount.
- **H4, acceptance:** the pin goes red with the fix reverted (ablation below).

### Real Chromium, after the fix (scratch probe, not committed)

The real `SettingsView` under a real `BrowserRouter` beside real `Link`s, served by the console's own Vite on a free port, over a stubbed settings API, driven by Playwright with Chromium 1194:

```
CANCEL sidebar link Business Units | url=/settings/localization | bar=1 unsaved change | box=FR | dialogs=["confirm: You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to leave?"]
CANCEL sidebar link Company (another namespace) | url=/settings/localization | bar=1 unsaved change | box=FR | dialogs=["confirm: ..."]
CANCEL All settings crumb | url=/settings/localization | bar=1 unsaved change | box=FR | dialogs=["confirm: ..."]
CONTROL same-page link | url=/settings/localization | bar=1 unsaved change | box=FR | dialogs=[]
CONTROL ctrl-click (new tab opened: /business-units) | url=/settings/localization | bar=1 unsaved change | box=FR | dialogs=[]
TAB CLOSE while dirty | page closed=false | dialogs=["beforeunload: "]
OK on Company | url=/settings/company | bar=(no bar) | box=Acme | dialogs=["confirm: ..."]
CONTROL clean page link | url=/business-units | bar=(no bar) | box=(no input) | dialogs=[]
RESIDUAL browser Back while dirty | url=/business-units | bar=(no bar) | box=(no input) | dialogs=[]
CONTROL tab close on a clean page | page closed=true | dialogs=[]
```

The same driver at the base commit (the BEFORE leg) read `dialogs=[]` on every departure: `url after=/business-units`, `/settings/company` with the box back to `Acme`, and `/system/settings`. With the tab close, the page closed with no prompt.

## Tests

New `apps/console/src/pages/settings/__tests__/SettingsView.leaveGuard-13163.test.tsx`, 12 tests. It drives the whole page under a real `BrowserRouter`, the router the console mounts, beside a stand-in sidebar of real `Link`s, over a stubbed `fetch`. `confirm` is a stubbed global because happy-dom's window has none. The prompt is asserted to be the bundle's `en.form.unsavedChanges`, which pins the key binding, not the wording.

On head `4f32cf4`, with `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 apps/console/src/pages/settings/` from the repo root under the shared verify lock: `Test Files 23 passed (23)`, `Tests 192 passed (192)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

**Ablation** (fix committed first, then `SettingsView.tsx` checked out at `c209c93` under a trap that restores from `HEAD`): the on-disk hits of `useUnsavedLeaveGuard` went from 2 to 0, and the bare `navigate('/system/settings')` crumb came back (1 hit). Result: `Tests 6 failed | 6 passed (12)`. The six that went red are the asks-first family (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`), the tab-close one (`expected false to be true`), and the unmount one. The environment control and the five controls stayed green, as expected. The restore was proved by the blob hash equal to `HEAD`'s and `git diff HEAD` at 0 lines.

## Gates (local, head `4f32cf4`, exit codes captured before any pipe)

- Closure build, `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...' --concurrency=2`: 34 of 34 successful (28 cached).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console lint`: exit 0. It reports 0 errors and 220 warnings, none on the new files. The two warnings on `SettingsView.tsx` are on lines this PR does not change, moved down one line by the new import.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`. A `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` run lists both new files in the program.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: exit 0, `0 new citation(s)`.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, 1 changeset for 1 released package.
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys`: exit 0.
- `pnpm check:i18n-drift`: not run. No string moves into the i18n table; an existing key gets its first consumer.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the four paths: NOT GOVERNED.

## Acceptance notes

- **Residual: browser Back and Forward (`popstate`).** It is measured above (`RESIDUAL browser Back while dirty`: no prompt, edit gone). `BrowserRouter` gives a page no veto, `useBlocker` needs a data router, and history workarounds were not built, per the dispatch. Carrier: none.
- **Residual: shell navigations that start from a button, not an anchor.** These bypass the anchor guard: the header's user menu items, the workspace switcher, and a sidebar item's design menu all call `navigate()` from a menu item. This is a code reading, not measured in a running shell (no backend was bootable here). It is the same gap the `ResourceEditPage` guard has. Closing it needs a shell-level "page holds unsaved edits" seam in `@object-ui/app-shell`, which is out of this card's scope. Carrier: none.
- **Observation, dormant:** the settings `child_pane` row renders `href="#/settings/CHILD"`, a hash-router-era link. Under `BrowserRouter` it only sets the hash and goes nowhere. No manifest in the objectstack tree declares a `child_pane`, so nothing reaches it. Not filed. Carrier: none.
- objectui#13146 (a refused save shows the server message verbatim) is queued serially behind this card on the same file. This PR leaves the save and refusal paths and their toasts untouched.

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)
